frameworkCheck.title: AP Computer Science A Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2025)
frameworkCheck.how: The 53 numbered CED topics (1.1–4.17) and their learning objectives, essential knowledge statements, and exclusion statements were read from the course framework in the current PDF on AP Central, and each topic is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions teach it. The questions stay inside the CED's Java subset: only int, double, and boolean primitives; no prefix or embedded increment operators; no designing of inheritance relationships; the String, Math, Integer, Double, ArrayList, File, and Scanner methods named in the CED's Java Quick Reference; and no writing of recursive code. The five computational thinking practices and twelve skills were read from the CED's practices table, and each question is tagged with the skill it mainly uses. The Clarifications and Corrections implemented as of August 2025 (https://apcentral.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/ap-computer-science-a-course-and-exam-description-clarification.pdf) were checked: they change front matter and resource links only, not course content. Every code listing was compiled and run with a Java compiler; the outputs behind the keyed answers are recomputed by tools/checks/recompute/computer_science_a.py.
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the AP Students course page and the CED's exam section (shares of the multiple-choice section), both checked 2026-11-16
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page and the CED (3 hours; students receive the Java Quick Reference): Section I, 42 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes (55% of the score), individual questions plus occasional sets of two questions. The CED gives approximate multiple-choice weights of 2–10% Design Code, 22–38% Develop Code, 37–53% Analyze Code, 10–15% Document Code and Computing Systems, and 2–10% Use Computers Responsibly. Section II, 4 free-response questions in 90 minutes (45%): Methods and Control Structures (7 points), Class Design (7 points), Data Analysis with ArrayList (5 points), and 2D Array (6 points). StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only; writing code by hand is practiced with College Board's released free-response questions.

skills.text: Determine an appropriate program design to solve a problem or accomplish a task.
Determine what knowledge can be extracted from data.
Write program code to implement an algorithm.
Write program code involving data abstractions.
Write program code involving procedural abstractions.
Determine the result or output based on statement execution order in an algorithm.
Determine the result or output based on code that contains data abstractions.
Determine the result or output based on code that contains procedural abstractions.
Explain why a code segment will not compile or work as intended and modify the code to correct the error.
Describe the behavior of a code segment or program.
Describe the initial conditions that must be met for a code segment to work as intended or described.
Explain how computing impacts society, economy, and culture.

differences: The AP Students page's unit topic lists are summaries; the CED's 53 topics are the required content and are listed per unit as framework topics. The page's Unit 4 list does not name text files (CED topic 4.6), which StudySprint teaches in Unit 4.

This CED (effective Fall 2025) organizes the course into four units, and its exclusion statements place designing and implementing inheritance relationships outside the course. Study materials organized differently may describe an earlier framework.
StudySprint cannot run code that a student writes, so the Develop Code practice is practiced only by choosing among given code; the AP Exam's free-response section requires writing Java by hand.
